item.title: Punakha
item.description: Punakha Valley, known for its rivers and fertile fields Punakha is a historically significant district located in western Bhutan. It is known for its pleasant climate, fertile valleys, and cultural importance. Punakha served as the capital of Bhutan until 1955 and continues to be an important religious and administrative center. Punakha Dzong Punakha Dzong, also known as Pungtang Dechen Phodrang Dzong, is one of the most impressive fortresses in Bhutan.

item.title: Wangdiphodrang
item.description: Wangdiphodrang, known for valleys and rivers Wangdiphodrang is a district located in western Bhutan and is known for its scenic landscapes, cultural heritage, and traditional lifestyle. The district takes its name from Wangdiphodrang town, which serves as the administrative center. Wangdiphodrang Dzong Wangdiphodrang Dzong is one of the most prominent landmarks in the district. Located at the confluence of the Punatsang Chhu and Dang Chhu rivers, the dzong has historically served as an important administrative and religious center.

item.title: Zhemgang
item.description: Royal Manas National Park in Zhemgang District Zhemgang is a district located in the southern part of central Bhutan. It is one of the country’s more remote regions and is known for its rich forests, wildlife, and natural landscapes. The district is less visited than many other parts of Bhutan, offering a quieter and more traditional experience. Geography Zhemgang is characterized by hilly and mountainous terrain covered with dense subtropical and tropical forests.
